title: Advantech On-Site Septic System: Aerobic Nitrification for Watershed Protection

locations.name: Westerly, Rhode Island (on-site project)
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly identifies the speaker as being at a project in Westerly, RI

summary: This This Old House Pro2Pro segment documents an on-site septic system upgrade near water resources in Westerly, RI. The host contrasts a conventional 1,500-gallon septic tank with an Advantech aerobic treatment system housed in a vault. The conventional design uses anaerobic digestion in a two-chamber tank, where solids are separated and ammonia/nitrogen byproducts can enter groundwater. The Advantech setup adds an aerobic stage with distribution ports, screens, and aerobic bacteria that oxidize ammonia to nitrogen, which is vented through a roof exhaust. The treated effluent then passes to a sand/gravel dispersion field contained by a PVC liner to protect below-grade wood and meet code. The video highlights practical considerations such as system access for maintenance and cautions about decks over the system. Overall, the presentation argues that the Advantech approach yields substantially cleaner discharge (in the order of ten times cleaner) and better watershed protection than a conventional septic system.
